newsitem.title: FINLAND: German buy makes Enso Europe's number two paper maker.
newsitem.headline: German buy makes Enso Europe's number two paper maker.

text.p: Finnish forestry group Enso Oy said on Monday it was taking over German newsprint and magazine paper maker E.Holtzmann, widening its product range and making it Europe's second largest producer of paper and board.
Enso's initial purchase, of a 50.4 percent majority in the German company for 1.8 billion markka ($346.2 million), would boost its overall annual capacity by 700,000 tonnes to 6.7 million.
That puts Enso ahead of Sweden's Stora , but still clearly behind its Finnish rival UPM-Kymmene , it said. @
"We are now ... in a situation where we can offer all the products that publishers need and we are also competitive in size," Enso CEO Jukka Harmala told a news conference.
The deal met a lukewarm reception in Helsinki, with Enso's stock off 1.00 markka at 42.50 in thin mid-afternoon trade.
Analysts said it positioned Enso better in Europe and some welcomed continued consolidation instead of new capacity.

But others felt the price -- which in terms of Enso's commitments to date would total three billion markka -- may be too high, saying the purchase would put strain on Enso's balance sheet at a time of uncertainty in paper prices.
Enso said the deal would lift its earnings per share this year -- it more than halved in 1996 to 4.50 markka -- and at some stage meet its targeted 12 percent return on investment.
"At least in 1997, it definitely will not," said Lars Kjellberg, analyst at Enskilda in Stockholm. "I think hardly anyone will reach that this year."
"The price seems high in the short term at least," he said. Enso said the price was cheaper than recent deals.
Holtzmann's sales in 1996 were about 2.46 billion markka and its operating profit was about 580 million markka, but Enso said that profit would fall this year along with paper prices. @
Holtzmann has mills in Karlsruhe and Langenbrand in southern Germany making newsprint, uncoated magazine paper and wallpaper base.
Enso said it was particularly keen to get Holtzmann's uncoated magazine (super-calendered) paper production, where Holtzmann's capacity was 340,000 tonnes per year, to complete its product range.

Enso, which in 1996 had net sales of 25.7 billion markka and an operating profit of 2.7 billion markka, said it also expected to achieve through the deal synergy benefits of about 170 million markka per year by 1999. @
It said it would continue to develop Holtzmann according to current plans, including a 300 million markka investment programme, adding it would defer other major investments.
Enso said it had an agreement with Holtzmann's owner -- German publishing house Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung -- to buy 39 percent more in the company for the same price per share.
The remaining 10 percent is held by private owners, and Enso said it may buy the shares but had no obligation to do so.
